zh_summary: 個人對AI的看法有點極端：Claude最終可能取代大多數軟體，包括Microsoft Office。為此，AI需要變得更容易使用。大多數人如果切換有點麻煩就會堅持已知方式。疑問AI是否在使用感覺如此直觀、幾乎無需學習時最有利可圖。
text:
My personal take on AI these days is a little extreme. I think Claude could eventually replace most of the software we use, including Microsoft Office.

For that to happen, though, AI needs to get much easier to use. If you’re even a little comfortable with computers, it doesn’t take long to learn how to use AI, and once you do, it makes a lot of things easier. But most people are happy to stick with what they know if switching feels like even a minor hassle.

I wonder if AI will be at its most profitable once using it feels so intuitive that people barely have to learn anything at all.

Growth is not inflation.

The Fed's models, and the Wall St training built on them, treat anything above 1.5 per cent growth as overheating. That speed limit was set in a decade of 1 per cent productivity growth.

The data says otherwise. Strip out shelter, a lagging measure of old leases, and core CPI is 2.0 per cent. At target. What's left is gasoline, a supply shock already rolling over.
In the 1990s, growth ran above 4 per cent and inflation stayed contained. 

Productivity is supply.

Hiking into a productivity boom chokes the investment creating the supply.

Growth is not bad. Growth is the answer.

BREAKING: S&P 500 is on track for a 4th consecutive week with a return of at least 2.5% in either direction, its longest such streak since the 2022 bear market.

By comparison, the record streak lasted 10 weeks during the 2008 Financial Crisis.

This comes as the S&P 500 is up +3.9% so far this week, following a -8.6% weekly return last week.

In the two weeks before last week's sell-off, the S&P 500 first declined -2.7% and then gained +2.5%.

This volatility is an exceptional opportunity.

zh_summary: （由 @BarbarianCap 轉發）閱讀 Tegus 上的實驗室研究員與超大規模雲端專家通話並建立 ANT 模型後，結論是 2027 年將相當瘋狂，$ANT 基本情境到 27 年底在訓練／RL 模型上的支出約為目前 Opus 5.5 級模型的 6 倍（考慮效率提升尤其 RL 後更接近 10 倍有效訓練）。對前沿 AI 持樂觀態度，因研究員仍有無法滿足的運算需求（訓練被推理服務所限）；討論平台期陣營（如編碼）與持續進步之辯，指出 ANT 與 OAI 訓練約佔 AI GW 的 20%，質疑投資回報以及客戶服務運算占比是否會從約 25% 大幅上升。
text:
I spent a little bit of time reading Lab researcher / Hyperscaler expert calls on Tegus and building an ANT model (+AI GW Model)

My conclusion is that 2027 is going to get pretty crazy.

I don’t think I wrapped my head around just how much $ANT is going to be spending on training.

Market rightfully reacted when learning how little ANT was spending on serving customers vs. training with their ~25% split. The implication when you roll fwd Compute / % mix to training is pretty eye opening.

My ANT base case is they spend ~6x more on training/RL models by end of ‘27 vs. the current / Opus 5.5 class model. When you factor in efficiency gains (esp on the RL side), it is probably closer to a 10x increase in effective training. I personally can’t fathom what that leads to.

A huge amount of the debate will come down to:
What does it mean for ANT (and not too too far behind OAI) to spend 10x more effective compute training models over the next year?

There’s a camp that believes meaningful chunks of intelligence tap out – that for something like Coding, everyone will plateau at a similar point and with not too much training / RL bc the models essentially know how to solve this problem..RSI helps you get to the plateau faster bc the models know how to solve that problem (argument from META researcher below).

I’m more bullish on the frontier and have extreme excitement about what 10x more effective compute to train models by the end of ‘27 could mean: my read of the researcher expert
